items.example_en: Excuse me, where is the train station?
items.note: 请问 opens any question to a stranger. In the south: 在哪里.

items.example_en: I'm looking for the metro station.
items.note: 在 before the verb marks the action in progress.

items.example_en: Is it far on foot?
items.note: 近 is near. 走路 means to go on foot.

items.example_en: Go straight ahead to the traffic light.
items.note: 一直 also means all along or continuously.

items.example_en: Turn left after the church.
items.note: 右转 is turn right. 了 marks the completed passing.

items.example_en: Turn right at the next junction.
items.note: 口 means opening or mouth: 路口, 门口, 出口.

items.example_en: Let's meet in front of the train station.
items.note: 站 means station or stop: 地铁站, 公交站.

items.example_en: How do I get to the nearest metro station?
items.note: 怎么走 literally means how to walk, used for any route question.

items.example_en: The shop is open until ten at night.
items.note: 店 marks businesses: 饭店, 书店, 花店.

items.example_en: There's a pharmacy next door.
items.note: 家 is the measure word for shops and businesses.

items.example_en: The bank is across the road.
items.note: 行 is háng here, not xíng. Same character, two readings.

items.example_en: I really like this neighbourhood.
items.note: The standard unit of Chinese urban housing, gated and self-contained.

items.example: 买一张到上海的往返票。
items.example_en: Buy a return ticket to Shanghai.
items.note: 张 is the measure word for tickets. 单程票 is one way.

items.example_en: The ticket office is on the ground floor.
items.note: In China 一楼 is the ground floor, as in American usage.

items.example_en: The train is at platform three.
items.note: 号 numbers things: 三号站台, 五号线.

items.example_en: Change to line two at the next stop.
items.note: You will hear this constantly in metro announcements.

items.example_en: We'll take the metro, line four.
items.note: 坐 for sitting transport, 骑 for bikes, 开 for driving.

items.example_en: You need ID to buy a ticket.
items.note: Chinese rail tickets are tied to an ID or passport.

items.example_en: The train is twenty minutes late.
items.note: 迟到 is for people being late, 晚点 for services.

items.example_en: Our flight has been cancelled.
items.note: 了 marks the change of state.

items.example: 路上堵车，我会晚一点到。
items.example_en: There's a traffic jam, I'll be a bit late.
items.note: Literally blocked cars.

items.example_en: I missed the last train.
items.note: A resultative compound: 错 wrong plus 过 pass.

items.example_en: Sorry, I got lost.
items.note: 迷 means confused, 路 road. 了 marks the new state.

items.english: what time is the next one?
items.example_en: What time is the next bus?
items.note: 班 is the measure word for scheduled services.

items.example: 您好，我订了房间，姓杜邦。
items.example_en: Hello, I've booked a room under the name Dupont.
items.note: 了 after the verb marks completion.

items.example: 我要一间有海景的双人房。
items.example_en: I'd like a double room with a sea view.
items.note: 间 is the measure word for rooms. 单人房 is a single.

items.example_en: Does the room rate include breakfast?
items.note: 包 here means to include.

items.example_en: Here is your room key card.
items.note: 卡 is a phonetic loan from card.

items.example_en: What time is check-out tomorrow?
items.note: 入住 is check-in, 退房 is check-out.

items.english: I'd like to cancel my booking
items.example: 我想取消星期五的预订。
items.example_en: I'd like to cancel Friday's booking.
items.note: 想 softens the request compared with 要.

items.example_en: There's a problem with the room's heating.
items.note: The neutral opening for any complaint.

items.example_en: The air conditioning is broken.
items.note: 了 marks the change from working to broken.

items.example_en: Could we change rooms?
items.note: 可以 is the polite may I or could you.

items.example: 行李可以寄存在前台吗？
items.example_en: Can we leave our luggage at reception?
items.note: 寄存 means to leave in storage.

items.example_en: Luckily I bought travel insurance.
Thank you for your understanding.
items.note: 您 keeps the register respectful.
